translation_notes: The region is a module-level statement acting on a free name `g`; context_shim.py binds `g` to a plain rdflib Graph parsed from fixture.ttl (in the real project it is the Query graph, a Graph subclass). Identical on both sides.

The three `g.subject_objects(P)` calls chained by itertools.chain become three `m{ ?s P ?o }` under `@graph g`, still chained (itertools.chain kept: the loop is not refactored). The three g.remove((s_, P, o)) with all three terms bound become three `-{ {s_} P {o} }` (no wildcard involved, so the 'received as data' pitfall does not arise); the add becomes `+{ {s_} dcterms:creator {o} }`.

Prefixes trimmed to the three really used (dc, dcterms, sdo); the draft's other 11 declarations were unused. SDO in rdflib 7.2.1 is https://schema.org/ - the fixture carries an http://schema.org/creator triple that must stay.

Fixture: dc/sdo creator and author on several subjects, a literal object, the same object under all three predicates, and neighbours (dc:contributor, existing dcterms:creator, http schema.org creator, sdo:name) that must not move. Verified non-hollow: the original removes 8 and adds 6 triples; dropping one `-{ }` line makes the check fail (12 vs 14 triples).
optimization_notes: optimized.py: chain() of three subject_objects becomes one subject_objects over the alternative path `DC.creator | SDO.creator | SDO.author` (rdflib evaluates the alternatives in written order, so the solutions and the last (s_, o) the module leaves are the same); the three removes become `g -= [... for p in (...)]` (a comprehension, so no module-level name is added to the compared values).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the path goes into the predicate position of one `m{ ?s {dc:creator | sdo:creator | sdo:author} ?o }`; the removes stay three `-{ }` (same token count as the `g -= [...]` line, and the specific island; a multi-pattern `-{ }` would join).
No exception to the symmetry: the path is a Python expression on both sides.
header_optimization_notes: Python: chain goes, and the namespace import keeps DC, DCTERMS, SDO of its fourteen names.
LD Python: chain goes; the three @prefix lines are used.
